name: Chinese nianhua New Year woodblock print
region: Yangliuqing (Tianjin), Suzhou, Weifang and other towns, China
summary: Workshops print a key-block outline and fill it with colour blocks, and often add hand-painted colour. Yangliuqing sheets end with hand colour and painted faces. Other towns print bold and flat.

philosophy.core_thesis: A New Year picture works as a charm for the house, so it must be bright, full of good signs and cheap enough for every door.
design_principles: Print a bold black key outline from a pear or jujube block. Keep the line 1–2 mm wide.
Use 3–8 colour blocks in vermilion, green, yellow and a late aniline magenta.
Fill the sheet with signs of luck: a door god, a fat child, a carp, a peony, a coin.
In Yangliuqing work, paint the faces and the hands over the print, with a fine brush and a white powder ground.
Add gold or lead-white on a robe or a flower, by hand, where the print needs a bright point.
Allow the colour to shift 1–2 mm from the outline. Keep the rough register.
Print thousands of sheets before the New Year, and paste them on doors and walls.
anti_patterns: A soft gradient or a pale, literati colour set
A clean vector line with no cut mark
A quiet, empty composition with no sign of luck

process.matrix: Blocks of pear or jujube wood, one for the outline and 3–8 for the colour.
process.press: No press. A printer rubs the back of the sheet with a pad by hand. Some towns add hand colour after the print.
process.image_making: Workshops split the work between the designer, the carver, the printer and the colourist, and hire out hand colour to village families.
process.edition: Thousands of sheets for each design, sold before the New Year.

inks.strategy: Water-based colour and ink. The outline prints first, then the colour blocks, and in some towns a brush adds colour over the print.

screening.rule: Make each tone a flat field of one colour, or a hand-painted tint. The style has no screen.

registration.rule: Allow 1–2 mm of shift between the colour blocks and the outline.

substrate.stock: Cheap paper, with a white powder ground in some towns.
substrate.finish: Unsized, with a thin, matt surface.

surface.impression: Light. The sheet is almost flat.
surface.sheen: Matt, with a small shine from the gold and the lead-white by hand.
surface.texture: Flat bright colour, hand-painted faces, and a rough paper fibre.

marks: gold and white by hand on robes

emotion.target_response: Loud, warm luck: the viewer feels a crowded, bright house at the New Year, with a charm on every door.

use_cases: Lunar New Year cards, packs and posters
packs for Chinese food and tea
avoid_when: The brief needs a quiet, pale or literati colour set.
The picture needs fine gradation or a photographic tone.

modifiers.how: Thin the line, use pale colour with a graded wash, and add a dry-block emboss on the petals.
Reduce the colours to four plant colours on a shell-powder ground, and drop the hand colour.
